name: Curve Heading
description: A card whose headline is laid out along a bell curve and flattens onto its own baseline as the card scrolls into view, then bends again with scroll velocity.

variations.name: default
variations.previewHint: Scroll the card in and out of view — the drooping headline flattens on entry, re-bows on exit, and bends with how hard you scroll
variations.description: The headline is not a straight line of text: every glyph is positioned by a Gaussian curve equation, distributed along it by arc length and rotated to its tangent. Perfect for marketing pages.

props.name: headline
props.description: The line laid along the curve. Split per glyph, so keep it to a short phrase that fits on one line.

props.name: copy
props.description: Body copy under the headline. Defaults to the built-in editorial paragraph.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the card itself.

props.name: scrollRoot
props.description: Scrolling ancestor to measure against. Left undefined the block reads the window and the viewport, which is what a real page wants. Point it at an overflow-y container and both the entrance trigger and the velocity bend follow that container instead.

props.name: hint
props.description: Optional nudge centred in the top runway, e.g. "Scroll me", with a pair of dots drifting downward beside it. The runway is a blank field of scene colour, so on first paint nothing tells you the card is below it. Left undefined the runway stays empty, which is what a real page wants.

features: The baseline is a Gaussian, y(x) = A·(1 − e^(−x²∕2σ²)), pinned so the middle of the word holds level while both ends droop away — flat tails, one smooth hump, unlike a circular arc
Glyphs are distributed along the curve by arc length, not by horizontal position, so the word bends without stretching — which is what makes the bowed line look elastically narrowed

Amplitude is the single degree of freedom: as it springs to 0 the curve, its tangent rotation and its arc length all collapse to the flat case, so the text realigns onto the browser's own centred layout with no per-glyph target positions anywhere in the file
Arc length is tabulated over 128 samples and inverted by binary search, memoised in a bounded cache keyed to a tenth of a pixel, so all fifteen glyphs sharing an amplitude solve the curve once
The entrance pose and the scroll-velocity bend are the same quantity and simply add, so one curve carries both
Scroll velocity is mapped through tanh rather than clamped, so ordinary scrolling actually bends the word instead of sitting far below a ceiling only a fling ever reaches
Both amplitudes tick every frame, so paints are coalesced onto motion's render step instead of writing each glyph's style twice per frame
`will-change` is written from JS only while the curve is bent — at rest the line is plain static text holding no compositor layer
A hand-rolled IntersectionObserver reports which edge the card is parked on, so the whole pose mirrors when you scroll back up: card from above, line falling, hump inverted
Respects prefers-reduced-motion — one multiplier collapses every travelling value at once, leaving the fade

Outer span holds each glyph's untransformed slot in normal text flow and the inner span carries the transform, so measuring and painting never fight; a ResizeObserver and document.fonts.ready re-measure after a webfont swap or resize
